newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS' BARRY SANDERS SIGNS REPORTED $34.5 MILLION DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS' BARRY SANDERS SIGNS REPORTED $34.5 MILLION DEAL.

text.p: Barry Sanders, who had threatened to hold out out if he was not given a contract extension, signed a six-year deal on Sunday worth $34.5 million, the richest contract for a running back in NFL history, ESPN reported.
A Lions'spokesman confirmed Sanders signed a contract Sunday, a week after training camp officially opened.
ESPN said saod the contract includes a signing bonus of $11.5 million.

The 29-year-old Sanders has rushed for 11,725 yards in his first eight NFL seasons. He has never had less than 1,115 yards in a season and has eclipsed 1,500 four times, including the last three years.
In 1996, Sanders led the league with 1,553 yards and became the first player in NFL history to rush for 1,000 yards in each of his first eight seasons.

The 1988 Heisman Trophy winner, Sanders is seventh on the NFL's all-time rushing list, trailing Kansas City's Marcus Allen by just 13 yards. Only Eric Dickerson and Jim Brown -- second and fourth on the all-time list -- reached 10,000 yards faster than Sanders.
Sanders is 5,001 yards behind all-time leader Walter Payton. At his current pace, he would overtake Payton, who ran for 16,726 yards, midway through the 2000 season.
In the off-season, the Lions fired coach Wayne Fontes, the only coach Sanders has played for, and hired Bobby Ross.

"I'm pleased that we were able to work this out and I'm happy to have Barry in camp," Ross said. "Now we have to get to work. He has some catching up to do, and I'm anxious to start working with him."
